rationale: C21 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both proclamations use the same distinctive sequence: identify a named exposition and its dates; cite a joint resolution authorizing the President, by proclamation or otherwise, to invite the States and foreign countries; explain that participation will promote foreign and domestic commerce and broader international benefits; and issue an invitation to those same participants to attend the event at the specified city and dates. C11 is also closely analogous, while C04 shares the international trade-and-participation machinery but less of the exact structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress by joint resolution approved July 27, 1956... has authorized the President... by proclamation or in such other manner as he may deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 28, 1954, authorized the President... by proclamation or in such other manner as he may deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim authorization recital, with only the resolution date and event changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: participation by the States of the Union and foreign countries... will contribute to our national welfare by promoting foreign and domestic commerce and by furthering harmonious and peaceful relationships
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the participation by the States of the Union and foreign countries... will advance the arts and sciences... and further foreign and domestic commerce
shared_material.explanation: Parallel policy-justification clause tying broad participation to commerce and additional public benefits.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate in the Oklahoma Semi-Centennial Exposition... from June 14 to July 7, 1957, inclusive
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby invite the States of the Union and all countries of the free world to participate in the First International Instrument Congress... from September 13 to September 25, 1954, inclusive
shared_material.explanation: Substantially identical operative invitation, adapted to a new event, location, participant formulation, and dates.
